# How to Get Visual Screenshots in Google Meet Notes (When Your IT Admin Allows It)

> **In short:** Google Meet's "Take notes for me" feature will soon paste screenshots of shared slides, diagrams and charts straight into your meeting notes document, so you stop guessing what was on screen. It's rolling out to Workspace customers in the coming weeks, and your IT admin needs to switch it on first.

Picture this: you hop out of a 45-minute client call, open the auto-generated notes, and… there's a tidy summary of what was said, but no trace of the slide deck the presenter clicked through for the last 20 minutes. You scroll back through your memory, then your email, then Slack, looking for the attachment. Twenty minutes gone. That gap is exactly what Google is trying to close.

The "Take notes for me" feature inside Google Meet already writes a transcript and a summary for you while the meeting runs. Now Google is adding **visual screenshots** — small images captured straight from whatever is being shared on screen (slides, charts, diagrams, whiteboard scribbles) — and dropping them into the notes document your AI assistant produces.

If you work in an office that runs on Google Workspace, this is the kind of small change that quietly saves you an hour a week. Here's what to know, and what to do about it before it lands.

## What "visual screenshots" actually means

Inside Google Meet, "Take notes for me" is an AI notetaker — think of it as a quiet assistant joining the call. It listens, writes a transcript, then hands you a tidy Google Doc with a summary at the end.

The new bit is simple: while it's writing those notes, it will also **snap screenshots of whatever is on the shared screen at meaningful moments**. Those images get pasted into the same Google Doc, right next to the moment in the transcript where they happened.

So instead of this:

> *14:03 — Maya walked through the Q3 pricing proposal.*

You get this:

> *14:03 — Maya walked through the Q3 pricing proposal.*
> [📷 Screenshot: Slide 4 — "New tiered pricing for SMB customers"]

That's the difference. The visual context travels with the words, instead of living in someone's head or a forwarded deck.

## Why it matters (and why you can't toggle it yourself)

A few things are worth knowing before you get excited:

- **It's not live for everyone yet.** Google has said the rollout is happening in the coming weeks. No firm date for general availability has been published.
- **Your IT admin controls it.** Workspace features like this aren't switched on by individual users — your admin turns the feature on (or off) for the whole organization, or for specific groups. If you don't know who that is, it's usually the person who set up your work email.
- **It only captures what is shared on screen.** If a presenter talks through a slide without sharing their screen, there's nothing to capture. The AI isn't reading the room — it's reading the screen-share feed.
- **It's an add-on to "Take notes for me."** If your meetings don't use that feature today, screenshots won't appear out of nowhere.

## What to do this week

You can't flip the switch yourself, but you can make sure the switch is ready to be flipped. A 10-minute conversation with your admin will save you weeks of waiting in the dark.

**Step 1 — Find out who your Workspace admin is.** If you don't know, open Google Admin Console (admin.google.com) and check the directory, or simply ask in your team chat: "Who's our Google Workspace admin?" It might be your IT manager, your head of operations, or an external IT provider.

**Step 2 — Send them a short, specific message.** Don't just say "turn on the new AI thing." Say what you want. Something like:

> *Hi [name], I saw Google is rolling out visual screenshots inside Meet's "Take notes for me" feature. Could you check whether it's available on our Workspace plan and, if so, turn it on for [my team / everyone]? Happy to be the guinea pig.*

**Step 3 — Check your own meeting settings.** Once it's enabled for your account, the next time you start a Meet call, look for the "Take notes for me" button at the bottom of the screen (the one with the little notepad icon). Tap it before the meeting starts, as you normally would.

**Step 4 — Ask presenters to share their screen during key moments.** This is the habit change. Screenshots only land in your notes when something is actually being shown. If a presenter talks through a slide deck in person or without screen-share, those slides won't appear. A quick "can you share your screen while you walk through that?" from the meeting host is all it takes.

**Step 5 — Review the notes doc after the meeting, not just at the end.** The screenshots appear in real time as the meeting goes on. If you spot a slide that's wrong or missing, you can ask the presenter to re-share it before the call ends.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Assuming the switch is on by default.** It usually isn't for new AI features in Workspace. Confirm with your admin before your first meeting.
- **Sharing confidential content without thinking.** Anything shown on screen during the call may end up in the notes document. Be mindful of sensitive dashboards, client data, or unreleased designs.
- **Skipping "Take notes for me" because you didn't see the prompt.** The button often appears as a pop-up before the meeting starts. Click "Allow" or "Start taking notes" — otherwise the screenshots have nowhere to go.
- **Treating the notes doc as a substitute for actually being there.** The AI summarizes and captures visuals, but it doesn't catch sarcasm, side conversations, or the vibe of the room. Read it, don't just file it.

## What this means for you

- **If you run meetings for a living (sales, training, project leads):** this is one of those small upgrades that compounds. Your post-meeting write-up time drops because the slides are already attached. You'll spend less time hunting for "the chart she showed at 14:03" and more time acting on it.
- **If you're a casual meeting attendee:** don't chase the feature. Wait for your admin to turn it on, then notice the extra images in your next notes doc. The summary will be the same — just richer.
- **If you're worried about privacy:** that's a fair instinct. Talk to your admin about whether visual screenshots should be enabled for external meetings, or whether certain teams (HR, legal, finance) should keep it off for now.

## Wrap-up

Google Meet's notes feature is about to stop being text-only. Once your Workspace admin enables visual screenshots, every shared slide and chart during a call will land inside the same Google Doc as the meeting summary — no more guessing what was on screen.

The move you can make today: find your Workspace admin, send them the short message in Step 2, and get your name on the early-access list before the rollout reaches your account.
